evaluation: Effectiveness Evaluation of Degree-Penalized Geodesic Embedding for HNSW Topology Deanonymization

sift10k.note: Degree penalty improves over unweighted geodesic by +0.108 R@10 (67% relative) but still below adjacency-only

msmarco10k.note: Degree penalty improves over unweighted geodesic by +0.143 R@10 (52% relative) and exceeds adjacency-only

decision_rule_application.proceed_criteria: Delta >= 0.10 on at least one dataset AND Delta >= 0.05 on the other, consistently across all 3 seeds
decision_rule_application.proceed_reason: SIFT10K delta is negative (-0.0791), so the dual-dataset improvement criterion is not met
decision_rule_application.pivot_criteria: Unweighted geodesic improves over adjacency-only but degree penalty provides no additional gain
decision_rule_application.pivot_reason: Unweighted geodesic does NOT improve over adjacency-only on either dataset. The degree penalty IS essential (provides +0.108 and +0.143 over unweighted). This does not match the Pivot scenario.
decision_rule_application.refute_criteria: Both geodesic variants improve Recall@10 by < 0.02 on both datasets
decision_rule_application.refute_reason: Degree-penalized geodesic improves by +0.0916 on MSMARCO-10K, well above 0.02 threshold
decision_rule_application.outcome_description: The degree-penalized method shows a strong positive effect on MSMARCO-10K (768-d) with +0.0916 improvement over adjacency-only, but degrades performance on SIFT10K (128-d) by -0.0791. The effect is dimension-dependent: the method works in high-d but not low-d. None of the three predefined decision outcomes (Proceed/Pivot/Refute) exactly applies.

verdict_justification: The experiment ran successfully on all configurations and seeds. There is a clear positive signal: the degree-penalized geodesic method recovers substantially more true kNN relationships than raw adjacency on the high-dimensional MSMARCO-10K dataset (+9.16pp, consistent across all 3 seeds with very low variance). The degree penalty is essential (unweighted geodesic alone underperforms adjacency-only on both datasets). While the method does not improve on low-dimensional SIFT10K, the high-d result demonstrates that topology-only reconstruction CAN enable meaningful additional kNN recovery, particularly when the embedding dimensionality is high and the adjacency-only baseline is weaker.
